quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left part of the lane, next to the centerline.
The right part of the lane, next to the curb.
It depends on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is best all the time. Choose the position that gives you the most visibility and space. Move your position as traffic conditions change.

questions.question: In general, what is the best position to ride in within a lane?

options.text: The left position
The right position
There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Good riders change their position as conditions change.

questions.question: Is it smart to use all three lane positions?

options.text: No, because you won't get used to any part of the lane.
No, because it confuses other drivers.
Yes, if you are adjusting to changing conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if you are adjusting to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best and no position should always be avoided. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Are helmets required?

options.text: Yes, for all riders.
No, but they are recommended.
Only for inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmets every time they ride. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in an accident.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers will see you as early as possible.
Stop at the sign or signal, then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and honk your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers will see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of the lane where other drivers will see you as early as possible.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This improves your vision and helps drivers in the next lane see your move.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If the rear wheel locks on a good surface, keep it locked until you stop. On good road surfaces, you can control the motorcycle with a locked rear wheel as long as it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, apply the front and rear brakes together and downshift.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
A signal is ahead.
Stop completely and then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic or pedestrians, and proceed when safe.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you apply the rear brake.
It knows when to brake automatically based on your habits.
It connects to the gears and brakes when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes when you apply the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle during normal riding?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on during the day and night whenever it is legal and safe. This includes your high beam and running lights. This is the best way to help others see your motorcycle.

questions.question: What should motorcyclists do about the oily strip in the center of a traffic lane?

options.text: Avoid riding on it.
Not worry about it.
Find the lane with the least amount of oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on it.
questions.explanation: Avoid the oily strip. The oily buildup is usually only about two feet wide. You can ride to the left or right of it and still stay in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull to the shoulder and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads become slippery when rain first starts, especially in the center of lanes. Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting it.
Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle you cannot avoid, slow down. Approach the obstacle at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: What should you do if you get a flat tire while riding?

options.text: Hold the handgrips firmly and do not use the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel and immediately pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly and do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and stay on a straight path. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Exit the road once your motorcycle has slowed down.

questions.question: What about the oily strip in the center of a lane?

options.text: It should always be avoided.
It usually has good traction, unless it is raining.
It should only be used when sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually has good traction, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip usually has enough traction for safe riding, unless it is raining. The oily strip is typically only about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: What should you do when being passed on your left?

options.text: Speed up.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center portion of your lane when being passed on your left. Riding on the right can be dangerous because it may make the passing driver move back into your lane too quickly.

questions.question: How can you avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Turn off your turn signal after completing a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after completing a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Always turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change. Leaving it on can confuse other drivers.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.

options.text: Louder than
Quieter than
About as loud as

questions.correctAnswerText: Quieter than
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as a car's horn. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it to keep you safe.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can most safely handle road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can most safely handle road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions one at a time, not together. Never brake while swerving. Braking and swerving at the same time can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: It gives you more time to react to hazards.
It prevents you from finding an escape route.
It gives you space to maneuver your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents you from finding an escape route.
questions.explanation: Space between you and the vehicle ahead helps you react faster if the other driver makes a mistake. It also gives you space to safely maneuver your motorcycle.

questions.question: Can two motorcyclists ride side by side in the same lane?

options.text: No.
Yes, but only if there is heavy traffic.
Yes, anytime.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, anytime.
questions.explanation: Two motorcycles can legally share the same lane and ride side by side. Motorcyclists are allowed to use the full width of one lane, and other vehicles cannot share that lane with them. But two motorcycles can ride together in one lane.

questions.question: What is the key to making a quick turn?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Lean your motorcycle quickly in the turn direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean your motorcycle quickly in the turn direction.
questions.explanation: The key to a quick turn is to lean your motorcycle fast in the direction you want to go. The sharper the turn, the more you need to lean.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group ride?

options.text: At the front leading the group.
Near the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch the less experienced riders at the same time.

questions.question: When it starts raining, where should you ride?

options.text: Leave the road and wait.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following you too closely.
When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as bright as a car's brake light. Flash your brake light when slowing or stopping so others see you are slowing down. This is especially important when you slow faster than others expect.

questions.question: Which is NOT a method to maintain control during a turn?

options.text: Speed up through the turn.
Slow down before turning.
Lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up through the turn.
questions.explanation: To stay in control, slow down before the turn. Look through the turn in the direction you want to go. Lean the motorcycle and smoothly increase speed through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: Before you start riding, the fuel valve should be:

options.text: Open.
Closed.
Covered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Make sure the fuel valve is open before you ride. If it is closed, the engine may start but will stall once the fuel remaining in the lines runs out.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, where should you ride?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride wherever you feel comfortable.
Ride on the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding on the left side of the lane is safest when passing parked cars. This helps you avoid hazards like car doors opening, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out. Always be ready to change your position based on road and traffic conditions.
